items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: The son, who was about my age, and I used to play together and I would go to his house very often and play the different piano rolls for hours.

ctx.x: Another event that used to take place on Kenyon Avenue, was a jug band that used to come around often and play in the streets and pass around a hat for people to put money in. There was a harmonica player, a big glass jug that one fellow would blow in and make it sound like a bass, and a violin player named Luther who could make his violin sound like it was saying "Oh Luther"...They made good money because everyone enjoyed their music and gave freely whatever they could afford.

There was a family by the name of James that lived a few doors from me that had a piano player. The son, who was about my age, and I used to play together and I would go to his house very often and play the different piano rolls for hours. Many people who could not play music had these type of pianos..I loved music but never tried to play the piano at that time.

There was also in the neighbourhood a boy who's name was Willis Ivy and who's mother made him take violin lessons but I was not interested in playing music and for me a violin was more of an instrument for girls, although I liked the way Luther played it. I never told Willis what I thought of the violin because we were good friends and did not wish to hurt his feelings.
